subject: Agriculture
title: Pigs and Intelligence
description: A quick win: understand Pigs and Intelligence.

hook.text: Pigs can learn their names, play video games with joysticks, and recognize human faces. They're surprisingly smart.

buildup.text: Domesticated 9,000 years ago in China and Turkey, pigs convert feed to meat more efficiently than cattle.

discovery.text: Pigs share 98% genome similarity with humans. Their organs are studied for human transplant research.

twist.text: Despite their intelligence, industrial pig farms confine sows in gestation crates too small to turn around in.

climax.text: The cognitive abilities of pigs fuel the strongest animal welfare debates in modern agriculture.

punchline.text: The smarter the animal, the harder the ethical question.

quiz.question: What makes the welfare of pigs particularly debated?
options: Their high intelligence and cognitive abilities
